In promptfoo, you can re-run only the errored test cases with the `--filter-errors-only` option on `promptfoo eval`. You pass it the ID of the earlier evaluation, or `latest`:

```powershell
promptfoo eval --filter-errors-only latest
```

or with a specific evaluation ID:

```powershell
promptfoo eval --filter-errors-only <eval-id>
```

This reruns only the cases that ended in an error, such as network failures or rate-limit responses, and skips the ones that passed or failed normally. The results are saved as a new evaluation.

I'm not fully certain of the exact flag names and whether they vary by version, so please check `promptfoo eval --help` and the promptfoo docs for your installed version. I also believe newer versions include a `promptfoo retry` command aimed at the same purpose, but I can't confirm its details. If you're hitting rate limits, you may also want to lower the concurrency (for example, with `-j` or `--max-concurrency`) before rerunning, so the same errors don't recur.
